correctness.rationale: For Z_n=s(x+n y+binom(n,2)alpha), all nonempty Walsh moments of up to three distinct times vanish: s has only odd nonzero Fourier frequencies, and Haar integration requires both sum k_j=0 and sum n_j k_j=0; three odd k cannot sum to zero. Thus four-word distribution depends only on C(alpha)=E product Z_0..Z_3. Translation alpha->alpha+1/2 and negation reduce alpha to d=dist(alpha,1/2 Z)∈[0,1/4]. Discontinuity hyperplane arrangement for 4 signs has only critical d=0,1/6,1/4, and signed polygonal area is quadratic between knots. Independently re-enumerated all 56 relevant planes and exact possible breakpoints; rational slice integrations at six phases confirm C=1/3-16d²+48(d-1/6)_+². The algebraic completeness argument then extends the finite exact computations to all real alpha. C vanishes iff d=sqrt(3)/12, with zero entropy from polynomial Bowen covering; independent checks do not assert generic higher-order independence.
